title: Higher concentration of extracellular vesicles in plasma from ME/CFS patients, with protein cargo alterations implicating complement and coagulation pathways
projectDescription: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a chronic and debilitating disease characterized by post-exertional malaise, fatigue and pain. Yet, its underlying biological mechanisms remain poorly understood. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoparticles carrying biological cargo and are involved in cell-cell communication. Plasma EVs reflect several disease states and may serve as minimally invasive biomarkers. We characterized the plasma EV profiles of ME/CFS patients (N=49) and healthy controls (N=50), by enriching for EVs by size-exclusion chromatography coupled to high-resolution quantitative proteomics.
sampleProcessingProtocol: EVs were lysed and precipitated on to magnetic hydroxyl beads (ReSyn Biosciences) by adding 70% Acetonitrile. After washing of the beads with 100% acetonitrile and 70% ethanol, proteins were reduced, alkylated before trypsin digestion and peptide purification. LC-MS/MS analysis was performed on a EVOSEPone coupled to a timsTOFfleX mass spectrometer (Bruker Daltonics, Bremen, Germany) via a CaptiveSpray ionsource.
dataProcessingProtocol: Protein identification and label-free quantitation (LFQ) was done using MaxQuant, version 2.4.3.0. Carbamidomethyl was set as a fixed modification and acetylation of protein-N terminal and oxidation were set as variable modifications. First search peptide tolerance of 20 ppm and main search error 4.5 ppm were utilized. Trypsin without proline restriction enzyme option was used, allowing two miscleavages. The minimal unique + razor peptides number was set to 1, and false discovery rate (FDR) was 0.01 (1%) for peptide and protein identification. Default settings were used for label-free quantitation (LFQ). The UniProt database containing ‘Human’ entries (2022) was used for database searches. Further analysis of the data was performed in Perseus v2.1.1.0.
